reviewer: bp-node.lisp:221-243 parses the file's grammar on the host: separator, key set, digit class, a 20-digit cap and silent empty lines. Repeated keys are last-wins, with no refusal. ACL2 sees only the two integers (fn-bpnp-configured-budgets). fnn-octets-string decodes as UTF-8 (io.lisp:185-186), so SBCL's Unicode-aware digit-char-p and parse-integer accept non-ASCII decimal digits. This breaks the 'ACL2 owns every decision' rule. The input is the operator's own local file, size-bounded at 256 octets, so the impact is small.
scenario: The host decides the file's grammar: separator, key set, digit class and the 20-digit length. It also decides duplicate handling (last row wins silently) and treats an empty line as acceptable. ACL2 sees only the two resulting integers (fn-bpnp-configured-budgets), so no ACL2 theorem covers the file. SBCL's digit-char-p and parse-integer accept non-ASCII Unicode decimal digits, so the host and any ACL2 or Python reader of the same file can disagree about what parses. A file with 'owner-backoff 5' twice is accepted, with no record of which row was used.
title: Host parses and validates the BP node budget file itself, against the rule that ACL2 parses external data
